2.2 The Victor Meyer Test (R-B-C Test): 1° ──► Nitrolic Acid (Blood-Red), 2° ──► Pseudonitrol (Blue), 3° ──► Colorless

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2. The Lucas & Victor Meyer Discrimination Tests
conceptBreakdown.title: 2. The Lucas & Victor Meyer Discrimination Tests

summaryBox.title: Diagnostic Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Lucas Test: 3° immediate, 2° in 5–10 min, 1° only on heating. Victor Meyer: 1° = Red, 2° = Blue, 3° = Colorless (R-B-C).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DIAGNOSTIC TEST SUMMARY
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
   LUCAS TEST                  VICTOR MEYER TEST            HOT COPPER CATALYSIS
   Conc. $\text{HCl}$ + Anhyd. $\text{ZnCl}_2$ Red $\text{P}+\text{I}_2 \rightarrow \text{AgNO}_2 \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2$ Vapors passed over $\text{Cu}$ at $573\text{ K}$
   (Turbidity of $\text{R-Cl}$)  $\rightarrow \text{NaOH} \implies$ **R-B-C Color**  ($1^\circ/2^\circ \to \text{Carbonyl}$; $3^\circ \to \text{Alkene}$)

                        VICTOR MEYER COLOR MATRIX
                        
   1. PRIMARY ($1^\circ$) ALCOHOL   ──► Forms Nitrolic Acid   ──► **BLOOD-RED COLOR**
   2. SECONDARY ($2^\circ$) ALCOHOL ──► Forms Pseudonitrol    ──► **BLUE COLOR**
   3. TERTIARY ($3^\circ$) ALCOHOL  ──► Lacks $\alpha$-Hydrogen    ──► **COLORLESS**
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **The Lucas Test**: $\text{R-OH} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhyd. }\text{ZnCl}_2} \mathbf{\text{R-Cl} \downarrow \text{ (Turbidity)}} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. $3^\circ$ gives immediate turbidity; $2^\circ$ in 5–10 min; $1^\circ$ only upon heating.
- **The Victor Meyer Test**: Alcohol $\to$ Iodide $\to$ Nitroalkane $\to$ Reaction with $\text{HNO}_2 \to$ Alkali addition gives Blood-Red ($1^\circ$), Blue ($2^\circ$), or Colorless ($3^\circ$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.3 Dehydrogenation Over Hot Copper (573 K / 300°C)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.3 Dehydrogenation Over Hot Copper (573 K / 300°C)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DEHYDROGENATION / DEHYDRATION OVER HOT COPPER (573 K):

• Primary (1°) Alcohol:   R-CH₂OH ──[Cu/573 K]──► R-CHO (Aldehyde) + H₂ ↑
• Secondary (2°) Alcohol: R₂CHOH  ──[Cu/573 K]──► R₂C=O (Ketone) + H₂ ↑
• Tertiary (3°) Alcohol:  (CH₃)₃C-OH ──[Cu/573 K]──► (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ (Isobutene) + H₂O (DEHYDRATION!)
conceptBreakdown.content: Passing vapors over metallic copper at $573\text{ K}$ dehydrogenates $1^\circ$ alcohols to aldehydes and $2^\circ$ alcohols to ketones, but causes **catalytic dehydration** of $3^\circ$ alcohols into alkenes (e.g., isobutene).

Victor Meyer: 1° = Blood-Red (nitrolic acid), 2° = Blue (pseudonitrol), 3° = Colorless.
Hot Cu (573 K): 1° ──► Aldehyde + H₂, 2° ──► Ketone + H₂, 3° ──► Alkene + H₂O (dehydration).
